title: Style Conventions
body:
Naming and layout rules that the interpreter does not enforce and the marker does. In [[Python]]
they are collected in PEP 8.

| Thing | Convention |
|---|---|
| Variable and function names | `lower_snake_case` |
| Constants | `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` |
| Indentation | 4 spaces, never tabs |
| Line length | keep it short enough to read |
| Names | say what the thing is: `total_price`, not `tp` or `x` |

**Indentation is the one that is not optional.** Python uses it to delimit blocks, so bad
indentation is a `SyntaxError` or a silently different program, not an untidy one. See [[Python]].

The rest matter for a reason worth stating once: **you write code for the next person to read it,
and the next person is usually you.** A first course grades style because the habit is cheap to
form now and expensive later, and because the same argument shows up again as
[[Coupling and Cohesion]] in [[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]] with more at stake.
Documenting *what a function is for* is [[Docstring]]; this note is about everything else.
